title: Representatives Move to Force Action on Gift Ban
raw_text:
Representatives Move to Force Action on Gift Ban
September 28, 2026
HARRISBURG – Reps. Mike Jones (R-York), Marc Anderson (R-York) and Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon) today filed a discharge petition trying to force the House of Representatives to take votes on
House Bill 744
, a measure that would prohibit lawmakers, political candidates and government employees from accepting cash in any amount and gifts valued at more than $50.
The representatives consulted with MarchOnHarrisburg advocates as they developed the discharge petition to uphold the organization’s mission to get money out of politics in Pennsylvania.
“We know that money can influence, there are reasons lobbyists spend it, and it can have a very adverse effect on the public’s trust and perception of our legislative body here in Harrisburg. Those things matter. They matter a lot,” said Jones. “While allowing for common sense exceptions such as legitimate education opportunities related to legitimate legislative work, this bill eliminates cash gifts and puts forth very substantial restrictions on personal gifts, such as travel, sporting event tickets, and individual meals, none of which are necessary for any of us to perform our job as legislators,” he said.
Barger explained a large part of why he supports the petition is because of overall inaction in the Pennsylvania General Assembly.
“The House has been in voting session just 36 days this calendar year. We’re supposed to be a full-time Legislature, but House Democrats have given us few opportunities to be in Harrisburg and even fewer chances to consider worthy legislation like the gift ban and the multiple bills that would protect female athletes from competing against males,” Barger said. “We shouldn’t have to force it to happen. Why are we not here more often doing the work of the people?”
“Servant leadership is a critical element of self-government,” said Anderson. “One cannot effectively and honorably serve the people if they seek to serve themselves. The ban on legislative gifts is a step to return our focus on service to others instead of service to self.”
Jones said it’s quite rare for Republican lawmakers to force a vote on a Democrat bill. “While our actions cannot force the bill into law, it can force action on the bill; and it can force some, hopefully all members, to finally let us know where they stand on the gift ban. It’s time for an up- or- down vote. That’s all we want,” Jones said.
Jones filed the discharge petition at the Capitol this morning ahead of its formal introduction in the House.
They held a news conference to announce their intentions
.
Representative Mike Jones
93rd Legislative District
Representative Scott Barger
80th Legislative District
Representative Marc Anderson
92nd Legislative District

title: Focus on Data Centers: Barger, Verobish Tackle Tough Issues at Joint Event
raw_text:
Focus on Data Centers: Barger, Verobish Tackle Tough Issues at Joint Event
September 24, 2026
ALTOONA –
Reps. Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon) and Andrea Verobish (R-Blair) today hosted an informational meeting about the anticipated proliferation of data centers across the United States, with a particular focus on how large-scale installations will impact the 13-state power grid that includes Pennsylvania.
Barger and Verobish addressed 200 constituents at the Blair County Convention Center, where they acknowledged concerns they’ve heard about environmental permitting, power and water usage, and the local controls established in statewide zoning laws.
Both representatives support the Ratepayer Protection Act – initiatives at both the state and federal level to ensure developers bring their own sources of new electric generation and meet other benchmarks.
“Sometimes it feels as if data center planning is outpacing sources of reliable information about the centers themselves. I’m thankful we could hold this meeting to share vetted, trustworthy information with our friends and neighbors,” Barger said.
“This next wave of development will require an all-hands-on-deck approach to ensure it is done responsibly,” Verobish said. “State lawmakers like us play a role, as do our partners in the federal government and local municipalities. Innovation and foresight are needed now more than ever.”

title: State Grant Funding Awarded Across Blair, Huntingdon Counties, Barger Says
raw_text:
State Grant Funding Awarded Across Blair, Huntingdon Counties, Barger Says
September 15, 2026
HARRISBURG — Local Share Account (LSA) grant funding has been awarded to five public safety, infrastructure and community development projects across the 80th District, according to Rep. Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon).
“Our local fire companies, police departments, municipal governments and healthcare providers are pillars of our region, and these grants strengthen the vital services they deliver every day,” Barger said. “Their work keeps our communities safe, connected and cared for. I’m pleased to announce projects that invest directly in the well being of residents of Blair and Huntingdon counties.”
“Securing funding for these projects strengthens public safety, improves emergency response, modernizes water and sewer systems, and ensures reliable municipal operations which will improve the quality of life for residents across the 30th district,” Senator Judy Ward said. “I’m pleased to have supported these grant applications, and grateful the CFA recognized their importance and awarded the funding.”
Approved projects include:
•	Blair County, $952,389 to purchase new mobile radios that will ensure reliable emergency communication for all 22 fire companies across the county.
•	Duncansville Borough, $65,844 to acquire a new police responder vehicle.
•	Huston Township, $600,000 to replace the deteriorated superstructure of Bridge No. 1 on Negley Spring Road.
•	Southern Alleghenies Planning & Development Commission, $175,000 to purchase and install a new digital X ray machine.
•	Warriors Mark Township, $150,000 to support construction of a new municipal building.
LSA grants are funded by state gaming revenue, not taxpayer dollars. The funding was approved by the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA). This is an independent agency that holds fiduciary responsibility over the funding of programs and investments in Pennsylvania’s economic growth.
Questions about the grants can be directed to Barger’s office at 814-695-2398.

title: State Grant Funding Helps Preserve 80th District History, Barger Says
raw_text:
State Grant Funding Helps Preserve 80th District History, Barger Says
September 11, 2026
HARRISBURG
— State grant funding has been awarded to two organizations working to preserve the history of the 80th Legislative District, according to Rep. Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon).
The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission (PHMC) awarded the grants through its Cultural and Historical Support Grant Program, which provides operating support to museums and historical organizations that preserve and share Pennsylvania’s heritage.
The Blair County Historical Society and the Huntingdon County Historic Society will each receive $9,500. The Blair County funding will help cover operational costs, including utilities and insurance, to support the Baker Mansion History Museum. In Huntingdon County, the grant will help pay for maintenance, conservation supplies and special exhibits.
“These grants support local historical preservation and enrich programming that serves residents and visitors alike,” Barger said. “Our county historical societies do a great job keeping history accessible, engaging and alive for future generations. I am glad to see their efforts supported by this funding.”
Questions about the grants can be directed to Barger’s office at 814-695-2398.

title: Blair Co. Projects Awarded Grant Funding, Barger Says
raw_text:
Blair Co. Projects Awarded Grant Funding, Barger Says
August 18, 2026
HARRISBURG – Three infrastructure projects in Blair County have been awarded grant funding through the state’s Multimodal Transportation Fund, according to Rep. Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon).
Bellwood Borough was selected to receive $473,000 to continue its streetscape work along Main Street. Antis Township will use $300,000 to extend the Logan Valley Trail to Lower Riggles Gap Road, while Woodbury Township will replace the Larke Road bridge with more than $1.2 million.
“These are important investments in rural infrastructure that too often can be overlooked. I commend borough and township leaders for seeking out this money to address work needed in our own backyards,” Barger said.
The Legislature created the Multimodal Transportation Fund in 2013 to address ports and rail freight, aviation needs, bicycle and pedestrian improvements, and similar projects.

title: Verobish, Barger to Answer Questions about Data Centers
raw_text:
Verobish, Barger to Answer Questions about Data Centers
August 17, 2026
ALTOONA
– Reps. Andrea Verobish (R-Blair) and Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon) will host an informational meeting about data centers Thursday, Sept. 24, from 6:30-8 p.m. at the
Blair County Convention Center
.
The representatives intend to share a presentation about the state’s preparation for the projected influx of data centers, with a specific focus on the centers’ power needs. They will answer questions after the initial presentation.
“Every day, we read a new headline about data center development somewhere in Pennsylvania,” Barger said. “Lawmakers are considering several proposals that affect that development. In particular, there is bipartisan agreement these developers need to provide their own sources of electricity.”
“Regardless of where these centers are built, they have the potential to greatly impact our regional power grid. Our constituents are rightfully concerned about these centers being incorporated into Pennsylvania via smart, deliberate development,” Verobish said.
Barring technical difficulties, the informational meeting will be livestreamed at both RepBarger.com and RepVerobish.com.
Those planning to attend at the convention center, 1 Convention Center Drive in Altoona, are asked to RSVP by Sept. 18 by visiting either representative’s website and clicking the “events” tab on the top. The RSVP form includes an opportunity to submit a question for the event.

title: Flood Victims Encouraged to Apply for State, Federal Assistance
raw_text:
Flood Victims Encouraged to Apply for State, Federal Assistance
July 23, 2026
HARRISBURG
– Residents and business owners impacted by the July 5-6 flash flooding may be eligible to take advantage of newly available state and federal disaster assistance, according to Rep. Scott Barger (R-Blair/Huntingdon).
The U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) has approved the state’s request for disaster loans for individuals, businesses and nonprofit organizations affected by flooding in Blair, Bedford, Cambria, Centre, Clearfield and Huntingdon counties.
In addition, the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency has activated the Commonwealth Disaster Recovery Assistance Program (DRAP) for eligible homeowners and renters in the City of Altoona, Antis Township, Logan Township, Snyder Township, Tyrone Borough and Warriors Mark Township.
“Our communities have shown incredible resilience in the wake of these devastating floods,” Barger said. “I encourage everyone who suffered damage to explore these assistance programs and apply if they are eligible. These resources may help with the recovery process.”
The SBA has also opened a Disaster Loan Outreach Center at the Tyrone Borough offices, 1100 Logan Ave., to provide in-person application assistance through Aug. 13. Copies of paper applications can be requested through Barger’s office by calling 814-695-2398.
Applications for SBA physical damage loans are due Sept. 21. DRAP applications (intended for filers with lower income levels) will be accepted through Oct. 21.
Residents with unmet recovery needs may also contact PA 211 by dialing 2-1-1 for additional local assistance and support.

80th Legislative District
